claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified now because aggregate launch readiness is above threshold, despite a current vendor-screening segment regression, on the theory that disclosure/monitoring can carry the remaining risk.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed before certification unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring comments may provide context but cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed acceptance.
evidence_requests: Current release model-card or release documentation showing the vendor-screening weakness is explicitly disclosed and the current evaluation results are reflected.
Approved risk-acceptance or reviewed mitigation record, with owner acceptance, covering the vendor-screening regression before launch.
Evidence showing the segment weakness is not material for the named launch use case, if that is the intended defense.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows a current material segment weakness in a named launch use case: the supply-chain vendor-screening slice is below the warning threshold.
The governing policy requires current-release disclosure of material limitations or approved risk acceptance before certification.
The record includes no attached current-release disclosure language reflecting this weakness.
The record includes no reviewed mitigation or approved risk acceptance covering the weakness.
Prior approval from three months earlier predates the current configuration/evaluation state and cannot satisfy the current-release requirement.
The informal monitoring note is contextual only and does not meet the policy threshold for certification.
unsupported_claims: That certification is currently supportable on the existing record.
That the present record is sufficient if certification is framed as contingent on documentation, when no admissible evidence shows the required documentation already exists.
That prior approval and informal monitoring materially close the current policy gap.
